episode_title: Stop the Burnout with Andy Robinson

real_qa.q: What does LFG Mindset Consulting stand for and why did Andy Robinson choose this name?
real_qa.r: LFG stands for 'Let's Fucking Go,' meaning we should be excited about everything we're after. Robinson chose the name because he wanted to capture the energy of athletes celebrating game-deciding moments—when a home run, touchdown, or three-pointer happens. His wife suggested the name, and it reflects the philosophy that we should bring that same celebratory energy to our everyday lives.
real_qa.requete: LFG Mindset Consulting meaning Andy Robinson

real_qa.q: How do real estate agents overcome the knowing-doing gap when they know what success looks like but don't take action?
real_qa.r: The gap exists because agents don't see themselves as the person who does the action and gets the result yet—it's about self-image. To close the gap, you must condition your subconscious through three elements: repetition (visualizing your future self daily in vivid detail), emotions (attaching strong feelings to those visualizations so your hippocampus registers them as important), and receptive state (being in a low-stress, meditative state rather than chronic stress so your brain can function effectively and receive the new identity).
real_qa.requete: knowing doing gap real estate agents mindset

real_qa.q: What specific technique can real estate agents use to train their subconscious to feel comfortable with new behaviors?
real_qa.r: The technique involves creating vivid mental representations of your future self doing the action. For example, Robinson writes in detail about taking his family to Chicago to watch baseball games, including sensory details like the taste of deep dish pizza and emotions of the experience, even though he hasn't done it yet. By repeating this daily with emotional intensity, you create the feeling of already being that person, which conditions your subconscious to accept the new identity and act naturally in that role.
real_qa.requete: subconscious conditioning visualization future self technique

real_qa.q: Why do high-producing real estate agents sabotage themselves when success is within reach?
real_qa.r: Agents sabotage themselves because they've built success through exhausting beliefs—that they must always be on, work weekends and nights, and never rest. When the business starts to take off and they're about to reach a payoff, the pattern of extreme effort becomes unsustainable. Building a relationship with your future self helps because that version of you doesn't operate under stress; your clients working with this framework achieve higher numbers but report it doesn't feel more stressful because it's aligned with how the elevated version of you naturally operates.
real_qa.requete: real estate agent self-sabotage exhaustion burnout

real_qa.q: How does releasing pressure and changing daily prospecting systems improve real estate agent performance?
real_qa.r: When an agent was required to have a specific number of conversations within two hours of calling or keep going indefinitely, it created unsustainable pressure. By releasing the attachment to that rigid structure and simply committing to two hours of calling every day regardless of conversation count, the agent started having better-quality conversations, stopped the cycle of skipping days, and attracted deals from multiple directions. The leading indicators (quality activities) created momentum that generated deals naturally rather than through forced effort.
real_qa.requete: real estate prospecting pressure systems effectiveness

guest.titre_secondaire: Former Vice President of Capital Markets
guest.bio_context: Andy Robinson is a former Marine Staff Sergeant and Purple Heart recipient whose life changed in 2006 when his vehicle was hit by an IED in Iraq, leaving him quadriplegic. He survived and rebuilt his life, moving into Capital Markets where he held the position of Vice President and built a corporate finance practice across New York and San Diego offices. He now works as a mindset coach with real estate agents through his company LFG Mindset Consulting.
